claim: EndoA1 and EndoA2 double knockout (KO) mice exhibit spontaneous epileptic seizures.
source: Previous studies found that EndoA1 and EndoA2 double knockout (KO) mice exhibit spontaneous epileptic seizures (Milosevic et al., 2011)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Milosevic et al., 2011

claim: Protein levels of endophilin A1 were higher in temporal neocortex neurons of temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) patients.
source: another study reported that the protein levels of endophilin A1 were higher in temporal neocortex neurons of temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) patients (Yu et al., 2018b)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Yu et al., 2018b

claim: In a chemical kindling mouse model of epilepsy, endophilin A1 was upregulated in the hippocampus and adjacent temporal cortex.
source: in a chemical kindling mouse model of epilepsy, in which mice are chronically induced with the GABAAR antagonist pentylenetetrazole (PTZ) (Dhir, 2012), endophilin A1 was also upregulated in the hippocampus and adjacent temporal cortex
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Dhir, 2012 and Yu et al., 2018b

claim: Silencing endophilin A1 expression in the hippocampal CA3 region reduced PTZ-induced seizure susceptibility and severity.
source: silencing its expression in the hippocampal CA3 region reduced PTZ-induced seizure susceptibility and severity (Yu et al., 2018b)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Yu et al., 2018b

claim: PTZ-induced epileptic behaviors were significantly exacerbated in EndoA1 KO mice compared with wild-type.
source: Compared with the wild-type, PTZ-induced epileptic behaviors were significantly exacerbated in EndoA1 KO mice (Figure 1A–C and Figure 1—video 1)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A-C

claim: EndoA1 KO caused a slight decrease in the amplitude of evoked excitatory postsynaptic currents (eEPSC).
source: We previously found that EndoA1 KO caused a slight decrease in the amplitude of evoked excitatory postsynaptic currents (eEPSC) and a significant attenuation of long-term potentiation (Yang et al., 2018)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Yang et al., 2018

claim: EndoA1 KO caused a significant attenuation of long-term potentiation.
source: We previously found that EndoA1 KO caused a slight decrease in the amplitude of evoked excitatory postsynaptic currents (eEPSC) and a significant attenuation of long-term potentiation (Yang et al., 2018)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Yang et al., 2018

claim: The eEPSC and its paired-pulse ratio (PPR) were not significantly changed in EndoA1 KO neurons.
source: Whole-cell patch clamp recording of CA1 pyramidal cells indicated that, while the eEPSC and its paired-pulse ratio (PPR) were not significantly changed
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data from whole-cell patch clamp recordings

claim: The evoked inhibitory postsynaptic current (eIPSC) was decreased in EndoA1 KO neurons.
source: the evoked inhibitory postsynaptic current (eIPSC), not its PPR, was decreased in the EndoA1 KO neurons
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data from whole-cell patch clamp recordings

claim: The PPR of eIPSC was not changed in EndoA1 KO neurons.
source: the evoked inhibitory postsynaptic current (eIPSC), not its PPR, was decreased in the EndoA1 KO neurons
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data from whole-cell patch clamp recordings

claim: Loss of endophilin A1 resulted in a significant increase in the E/I ratio.
source: resulting in a significant increase in the E/I ratio (Figure 1E–I)
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 1E-I

claim: Neither the frequency nor the amplitude of miniature EPSCs (mEPSC) was altered in EndoA1 KO neurons.
source: Of note, neither the frequency nor the amplitude of miniature EPSCs (mEPSC) or miniature IPSCs (mIPSC) was altered in EndoA1 KO neurons (Figure 1J–O)
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 1J-O

claim: Neither the frequency nor the amplitude of miniature IPSCs (mIPSC) was altered in EndoA1 KO neurons.
source: Of note, neither the frequency nor the amplitude of miniature EPSCs (mEPSC) or miniature IPSCs (mIPSC) was altered in EndoA1 KO neurons (Figure 1J–O)
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 1J-O

claim: Neither fast mIPSCs (perisomatic events) nor slow mIPSCs (distal dendritic events) were affected by EndoA1 KO.
source: Moreover, neither fast mIPSCs (perisomatic events:<2.8 ms) nor slow mIPSCs (distal dendritic events:>2.8 ms) (Miles et al., 1996) were affected by EndoA1 KO (Figure 1—figure supplement 1)
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1

claim: Presynaptic quantal release of soma- or dendrite-targeting inhibitory synapses is normal in EndoA1 KO neurons.
source: indicating that presynaptic quantal release of soma- or dendrite-targeting inhibitory synapses is normal
evidence: The claim is inferred from the mIPSC data showing no changes in frequency or amplitude

claim: Endophilin A1 in hippocampal pyramidal neurons functions in inhibitory synaptic transmission to maintain E/I balance.
source: these data indicate that endophilin A1 in hippocampal pyramidal neurons functions in inhibitory synaptic transmission to maintain E/I balance
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined electrophysiological data showing decreased eIPSC and increased E/I ratio

claim: There was a significant decrease in fluorescent signals of both VGAT and gephyrin in all subregions of the hippocampus of Sh3gl2-/- mice on postnatal day 21 (P21).
source: Analysis of confocal microscopy images revealed that, compared with the wild-type, there was a significant decrease in fluorescent signals of both VGAT and gephyrin, the inhibitory pre- and post-synaptic markers, or VGLUT1 and PSD95, the excitatory pre- and postsynaptic markers, in all subregions of the hippocampus of the Sh3gl2-/- mice on postnatal day 21 (P21) (Figure 2A, C, D, F, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, C, D, F)
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 2

claim: There was a significant decrease in fluorescent signals of VGLUT1 and PSD95 in all subregions of the hippocampus of Sh3gl2-/- mice on postnatal day 21 (P21).
source: Analysis of confocal microscopy images revealed that, compared with the wild-type, there was a significant decrease in fluorescent signals of both VGAT and gephyrin, the inhibitory pre- and post-synaptic markers, or VGLUT1 and PSD95, the excitatory pre- and postsynaptic markers, in all subregions of the hippocampus of the Sh3gl2-/- mice on postnatal day 21 (P21) (Figure 2A, C, D, F, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, C, D, F)

claim: A slight reduction in excitatory presynaptic protein was observed in Sh3gl2-/- mice at P60.
source: While a slight reduction in excitatory presynaptic protein was observed, the decreases in inhibitory but not excitatory postsynaptic proteins were also detected in the Sh3gl2-/- mice at P60 (Figure 2B, C, E, F, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B, C, E, F)
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 2

claim: Decreases in inhibitory but not excitatory postsynaptic proteins were detected in Sh3gl2-/- mice at P60.
source: While a slight reduction in excitatory presynaptic protein was observed, the decreases in inhibitory but not excitatory postsynaptic proteins were also detected in the Sh3gl2-/- mice at P60 (Figure 2B, C, E, F, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B, C, E, F)
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 2

claim: The assembly and/or stabilization of inhibitory postsynapses was impaired throughout brain development in Sh3gl2-/- mice.
source: indicating that the assembly and/or stabilization of inhibitory postsynapses was impaired throughout brain development
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation of decreased inhibitory postsynaptic proteins at both P21 and P60

claim: Gephyrin signals in all layers of the different hippocampal subregions were reduced in Sh3gl2-/- mice.
source: Notably, gephyrin signals in all layers of the different hippocampal subregions were reduced in the Sh3gl2-/- mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G and H)
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1G and H

claim: Decreased endogenous PSD95 or gephyrin clusters at synapses were visualized by recombinant probes in EndoA1 KO neurons in the CA1 region at P21.
source: In line with the data from immunofluorescent labeling (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1), decreased endogenous PSD95 or gephyrin clusters at synapses were also visualized by the recombinant probes, PSD95.FingR-eGFP or mRuby2-gephyrin.FingR, respectively (Bensussen et al., 2020; Gross et al., 2013), in EndoA1 KO neurons in the CA1 region at P21 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–D)

claim: Signals of the GABAAR γ2 subunit were decreased in the hippocampi of both juvenile and adult Sh3gl2-/- mice.
source: signals of the GABAAR γ2 subunit were decreased in the hippocampi of both juvenile and adult Sh3gl2-/- mice (Figure 2G–I)
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 2G–I

claim: Endophilin A1 orchestrates the assembly of inhibitory synapses, particularly the architecture of inhibitory postsynapses.
source: These data collectively indicate that endophilin A1 orchestrates the assembly of inhibitory synapses, the architecture of inhibitory postsynapses in particular, and functioning of GABAergic synapses
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined data showing decreased inhibitory synaptic markers and GABAARs

claim: The fluorescence signal intensity and number of surface GABAAR γ2 clusters were largely lower in dendrites of EndoA1 KO neurons.
source: the fluorescence signal intensity and number of surface GABAAR γ2 clusters were largely lower in dendrites of EndoA1 KO neurons, which was rescued by re-expression of endophilin A1 (Figure 3A–D)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3A–D

claim: The decrease in surface GABAAR γ2 clusters in EndoA1 KO neurons was rescued by re-expression of endophilin A1.
source: the fluorescence signal intensity and number of surface GABAAR γ2 clusters were largely lower in dendrites of EndoA1 KO neurons, which was rescued by re-expression of endophilin A1 (Figure 3A–D)
evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiment data shown in Figure 3A–D

claim: There was no change in surface GluA1 in EndoA1 KO neurons.
source: While no changes in surface GluA1 was detected, the fluorescence signal intensity and number of surface GABAAR γ2 clusters were largely lower in dendrites of EndoA1 KO neurons
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data

claim: There was no change in total levels of synaptic proteins in EndoA1 KO pyramidal neurons.
source: Biotinylation assay of surface proteins revealed that, compared with wild-type, although there was no change in total levels of synaptic proteins in EndoA1 KO pyramidal neurons
evidence: The claim is supported by biotinylation assay data shown in Figure 3E and F

claim: The surface expression of GABAARs was significantly reduced in EndoA1 KO pyramidal neurons.
source: the surface expression of GABAARs but not NL2 or the NR1 subunit of the NMDA-type glutamate receptor was significantly reduced (Figure 3E and F)

claim: The surface expression of NL2 was not significantly reduced in EndoA1 KO pyramidal neurons.
source: the surface expression of GABAARs but not NL2 or the NR1 subunit of the NMDA-type glutamate receptor was significantly reduced (Figure 3E and F)
evidence: The claim is supported by biotinylation assay data shown in Figure 3E and F

claim: The surface expression of the NR1 subunit of the NMDA-type glutamate receptor was not significantly reduced in EndoA1 KO pyramidal neurons.
source: the surface expression of GABAARs but not NL2 or the NR1 subunit of the NMDA-type glutamate receptor was significantly reduced (Figure 3E and F)
evidence: The claim is supported by biotinylation assay data shown in Figure 3E and F

claim: Postsynaptic endophilin A1 enhances the surface clustering of GABAARs and facilitates the assembly of inhibitory postsynapses in pyramidal neurons.
source: Collectively, these data indicate that postsynaptic endophilin A1 enhances the surface clustering of GABAARs and facilitates the assembly of inhibitory postsynapses in pyramidal neurons

claim: Endophilin A1 exhibits partial colocalization with gephyrin in dendrites of hippocampal neurons.
source: By immunofluorescence staining and super-resolution microscopy of hippocampal neurons in dissociated culture, we observed partial colocalization of endophilin A1 with gephyrin as well as surface GABAAR γ2 in dendrites of hippocampal neurons

claim: Endophilin A1 exhibits partial colocalization with surface GABAAR γ2 in dendrites of hippocampal neurons.
source: By immunofluorescence staining and super-resolution microscopy of hippocampal neurons in dissociated culture, we observed partial colocalization of endophilin A1 with gephyrin as well as surface GABAAR γ2 in dendrites of hippocampal neurons

claim: Endophilin A1 exhibits juxtaposition or partial colocalization with VGAT puncta.
source: and juxtaposition or partial colocalization of endophilin A1 and VGAT puncta (Figure 3G–I and Figure 3—video 1–3)

claim: Approximately 47% puncta of gephyrin or Bassoon were proximal to endophilin A1.

claim: The mean distance between endophilin A1- and gephyrin-positive pixels is approximately 120 nm.

claim: Endophilin A1 localizes to both ePSD and iPSD.

claim: Synaptic GABAARs contain the γ2 subunit along with α and β subunits.

claim: The levels of GABAAR γ2 and gephyrin were reduced at synapses in adult EndoA1 KO mice.

claim: Endophilin A1 functions at the iPSD to promote the assembly and/or stabilization of the GABAergic postsynaptic machinery.

claim: Gene Ontology analysis revealed that proteins related to glutamatergic, dopaminergic, and GABAergic synapses were identified as endophilin A1-interacting proteins.
source: Gene Ontology (GO) analysis revealed that, in addition to proteins participating in known cellular processes involving endophilin A1, such as synaptic vesicle recycling, actin cytoskeleton remodeling, endocytosis, and long-term potentiation (Gad et al., 2000; Ringstad et al., 1999; Schuske et al., 2003; Verstreken et al., 2003; Yang et al., 2021; Yang et al., 2018; Yang et al., 2015), proteins related to not only glutamatergic but also dopaminergic and GABAergic synapses were also identified, including gephyrin (Figure 4B and Supplementary file 1)

claim: Gephyrin was identified as an endophilin A1-interacting protein by mass spectrometry.
source: proteins related to not only glutamatergic but also dopaminergic and GABAergic synapses were also identified, including gephyrin (Figure 4B and Supplementary file 1)

claim: Endophilin A1 interacts with gephyrin but not NL2 in HEK293T cells.

claim: Co-immunoprecipitation from mouse brain lysates corroborated interaction between endophilin A1 and gephyrin but not GABAAR α1 or γ2.

claim: Neither endophilin A2 nor A3 interacted with gephyrin.

claim: The expression levels of gephyrin were not affected by ablation of Sh3gl2.

claim: There were no obvious changes in PSD95.FingR-eGFP clusters in dendrites of mature cultured hippocampal neurons following Sh3gl2 depletion.

claim: Immunofluorescence staining revealed a decrease in the clustering of gephyrin across the soma, the axon initial segment (AIS), and dendrites in EndoA1 KO neurons.

claim: Overexpression of endophilin A1 caused an increase in the mean signal intensity and number of gephyrin puncta in the soma and dendrites.

claim: Depletion of endophilin A1 caused a decrease in the localization of GABAAR γ2 to gephyrin puncta in EndoA1 KO neurons.

claim: Overexpression of endophilin A1 enhanced clustering of GABAAR γ2 in the soma and dendrites.

claim: The decreases in clustering of GABAAR γ2 in EndoA1 KO neurons were not rescued by expression of endophilin A1 fragments.
